STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white square-ish plate with a rim band and a flat centre, no inner wall or shadow. Flat plate (square).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: square plates are 20-30 cm. This plate looks like a large dinner-size square, so about 25 cm.
b) Reference: the broccoli florets are about 4 cm. Across the plate's flat centre, the broccoli and food span roughly 6-7 floret lengths, but the plate width is about 2.5-3 times the length of the salad mound (the salad mound spans roughly a third of the plate width). Estimating the plate at about 6-6.5 florets across gives roughly 24-26 cm.
Reconciled width: 25 cm, area = 625 cm2.

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Penne pasta with mushroom/chicken-type sauce (left half): covers about 35% of the plate, roughly 220 cm2. Mound average thickness about 1.5 cm (pasta and meat pieces stacked 2-3 deep at the centre, averaging below peak). Volume = 220 x 1.5 = 330 ml. Pasta and meat mixture, use 0.9 g/ml blended: about 300 g total for the pasta and sauce portion. Split: pasta about 180 g, meat with sauce about 120 g.
- Meat pieces (beef/chicken strips in brown sauce): about 120 g, cooked meat density 1.0, kcal around 180 per 100 g (sauce included, moderately fatty).
- Cooked penne pasta: 180 g, about 130 kcal per 100 g.
- Mixed salad greens (spinach and leaves) on right: about 35% of plate, 220 cm2, loose leaves 3 cm average. Volume 660 ml x 0.15 = 100 g raw leaves.
- Broccoli florets: about 6 florets, roughly 4 cm each, about 40 g total cooked-equivalent; use 40 g, about 35 kcal per 100 g.
- Carrot pieces and egg/cherry tomato accents: about 25 g carrot, about 40 kcal per 100 g; one egg-white wedge about 20 g, about 60 kcal per 100 g.
- Dressing/oil on salad: a small amount, about 5 g, about 450 kcal per 100 g.

Hidden food: no clear base beyond the pasta mound and the greens; no extra layer added.

Totals: pasta 180 g, meat and sauce 120 g, salad greens 100 g, broccoli 40 g, carrot 25 g, egg 20 g, dressing 5 g, total about 490 g.
